CANONICAL ROLL/DODGE-ROW PROMPT — one image, landscape 1536x1024, SIDE VIEW
ONLY. Fill {CHARACTER} from the game's art-style.json (including its
lockedDetails). Unlike the walk and attack prompts this file has no FRONT ROW
or BACK ROW block — a dodge-roll is drawn side-on ONLY and reused (mirrored,
and replayed for vertical dodges too) rather than drawn three ways. See
CHARACTER_SHEETS.md's "Roll / dodge" section for why. `generate_row.py --kind
roll --view side` fills this in for you; asking for --view front or --view
back fails on purpose, because there is no block for it to use.

---8<--- PROMPT STARTS ---8<---

A 16-bit SNES-style PIXEL ART sprite row on a SOLID FLAT PURE WHITE background (#FFFFFF, completely uniform). Exactly THREE sprites side by side in the middle of the image, evenly spaced, with a wide empty white margin on all four sides and a clear white gap between them — nothing touching, overlapping, or cut off by any edge. All three are the SAME character at the SAME size and the SAME pixel scale.

THE CHARACTER, drawn identically in all three frames: {CHARACTER}

{VIEW}

THE THREE FRAMES ARE ONE SIDEWAYS BARREL-ROLL, a silly, cartoony tumble used as a dodge move — left to right. FRAME 1 = TUCK, crouching low and curling into a ball just before going over, knees bent, arms pulled in. FRAME 2 = MID-ROLL, the biggest and silliest pose of the three: the whole body curled sideways and rolled up onto its side, tumbling through the air like a rolled-up armadillo, limbs tucked in tight, momentarily upside-down or on its back is exactly right here — this is the frame that has to read as "rolling", not just "crouching". FRAME 3 = RECOVER, popping back up out of the tuck onto both feet, momentum settling, back to a normal standing height.

This is a COMEDY dodge-roll, not a combat roll: exaggerate the tumble, keep it goofy rather than heroic.

ART STYLE: chunky flat cartoon pixel art, big simple shapes, flat solid colours, a thick black outline, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no dithering, no texture inside a colour block. Draw NO GROUND — no floor line, no bar or plinth under the feet, no platform, no shadow; the character floats on empty white and the game draws its own floor. Nothing else in the image: no grid lines, no boxes, no frames, no labels, no text, no numbers. FINAL CHECK, THE BACKGROUND: every pixel that is not one of the three sprites is PURE WHITE #FFFFFF. No backdrop, no vignette, no dark or coloured surround, no gradient, no scene, no border, no panel behind the characters. This is stated twice on purpose: a row that comes back on a dark or gradient background cannot be cut out and is rejected, and it is the failure that has wasted the most generations.

---8<--- PROMPT ENDS ---8<---


{VIEW} = SIDE ROW
-----------------
THE VIEW: all three sprites in strict SIDE PROFILE, facing RIGHT before the roll starts and after it ends (frames 1 and 3) — head in profile, nose pointing right, one shoulder to the viewer. Frame 2, the mid-roll, is the one frame allowed to depart from a clean profile — it is tumbling, so a curled, rolled silhouette read side-on is correct even where an exact profile isn't possible mid-tumble. The character's defining feature (mohawk, hat, horns) should still be readable in frame 2 if at all possible, same as it must survive an attack swing, but a roll is the one animation where it is allowed to be partly tucked away — it is upside-down for a beat, that is the joke.
